LESSON: WRITING 7.4.1 MECHANICS OF WRITING

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 7
Topic 7.4: Writing 7.4.1 Mechanics of writing
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 7.4.1 Mechanics of writing, part of Strand 7 in Grade 6 ENGLISH LANGUAGE.

Key inquiry question: Why should we punctuate our speech or writing correctly? 2. Which punctuation marks do you use frequently?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Collaboration: The learner’s ability to collaborate and carry out activities with peers is enhanced as they create a

poster or PowerPoint presentation and display the work to another group.

Creativity: The learner’s artistic prowess is developed as they make posters or PowerPoint presentations and

document successes made during recitations.

Values:
Love: It is cultivated as the learner learns to resolve conflicts while collaborating with peers to determine the

correctness of tense in sample sentences.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Information Technology: The learner interacts with technology and learns more about emerging trends as they recite

poems on scientific innovations paying attention to the use of the comma and the double quotation marks.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The skill of correct use of punctuation marks is critical when writing essays in other learning areas such as Kiswahili

and Religious Education.
